jobs.title: Director, AI Architecture & Agent Platform
jobs.description:
Position Summary

TKO Group Holdings, the parent of UFC, WWE, IMG, On Location and PBR, is deploying AI across multiple business units and a growing number of platforms.
The Director, AI Architecture & Agent Platform sets TKO's technical architecture for agents and AI platforms. This role determines how agents are designed, connected, evaluated, secured, observed and operated across TKO. It owns the technical point of view on orchestration, reusability, interoperability and platform choice, including where TKO should build, buy, use a platform-native capability or use an independent layer.
The role validates the architecture through targeted reference builds, including the first cross-system agent taken to production, then enables engineering and business-unit teams to deliver against reusable standards. It is not a central application delivery role or a high-volume build service.

This is an architecture-led individual-contributor role. It requires enough hands-on depth to prototype critical paths and challenge technical claims, along with the judgment and influence to guide work through teams that do not report to this role.

Responsibilities

1. Agentic Harness and Orchestration Architecture

Own TKO's technical point of view on where orchestration and reusability should sit, including build versus buy and platform-native versus independent options.
Define what each option requires, what it forecloses, and how agents built on different platforms will interoperate.
Lead the TKO-side answer to the initial orchestration assessment, working with an external partner while challenging the analysis and making the recommendation.
Define portability and migration criteria for platform-specific agents, including how TKO separates business logic, prompts, tools, identity, data access and evaluation from any one platform. Establish a path to rehost or retire agents built on IBM Watson, Salesforce or other platforms when warranted.
Establish the architecture principles and decision records that keep the agent platform coherent as the estate grows.

2. Reference Architecture and Technical Validation

Lead the architecture and technical direction for the first cross-system agent built through the new standard and taken to production.
Personally prototype or implement the critical parts needed to validate the architecture, then partner with delivery teams on the broader build.
Produce the templates, reusable components and engineering patterns that later builds will use.
Make the first-of-a-kind patterns real without becoming the long-term application owner or central delivery team for every use case.

3. Technical Evaluation, Estimation and Portfolio Input

Assess AI tooling and proposed solutions on technical merit at a level that can withstand challenge from engineers and vendors.
Provide architecture, feasibility, effort, total-cost and technical-risk input into portfolio prioritization.
Write technical assessments that make vendor claims, dependencies, limitations and tradeoffs explicit.
Identify when a capability should be adopted, piloted, built, deferred or retired.

4. AI Engineering Standards, Guardrails and Sandboxes

Define what must be true before an agent reaches production, including identity and access, evaluation and regression testing, observability, cost controls and failure handling.
Define standards for agents that take consequential actions, including payments or writes to source systems: authorization, human approval, segregation of duties, transaction limits, audit trails, idempotency, rollback and failure handling, data protection and testing. Own the AI architecture standard while platform, payment, security and business owners retain responsibility for their underlying controls.
Design and operate controlled sandboxes for emerging models and tools, including video-gen models such as Seedance. Give teams a safe way to test approved use cases without exposing TKO data, talent likeness, intellectual property or production systems.
Advise Engineering teams adopting tools such as Claude Code on repository and data access, secrets, code review, testing, dependency and intellectual-property controls, logging, cost limits and approved use.
Serve as the technical counterpart to Cybersecurity and other functions adopting AI tools. Help assess proposed uses, define safe operating practices, capture reusable patterns and align local decisions with TKO's enterprise architecture and guardrails.
Set the access controls, logging, spend limits, data and content rules, evaluation requirements and path to production or shutdown for those sandboxes.
Maintain an architecture decision and exception process: document the standard, approve deviations with named owners and expiry dates, and escalate unresolved cross-functional decisions with a recommendation.
Define the production lifecycle for agents and AI tools, including incident response, provider outages, model and version changes, material regressions and retirement, with clear handoffs to IT, Cybersecurity and business owners.

Role Boundaries

This role owns TKO's AI architecture, technical standards, reference patterns and architecture decisions.
Platform owners and Engineering own implementation and operation of their platforms. IT owns infrastructure, provisioning and service delivery.
Cybersecurity, Legal, Finance and Privacy retain ownership of their underlying controls and approvals. This role provides the AI-specific architecture and technical standard they apply.
Business units own local use cases, adoption and business outcomes. This role helps them use common patterns and decides when a local solution should become an enterprise pattern.

Required Qualifications

Experience architecting and operating agentic systems in production, not just prototypes, with a clear understanding of what failed, why it failed and how it was fixed.
Hands-on experience with orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph or LangChain, Model Context Protocol (MCP), tool-calling patterns and retrieval architectures.
Experience designing identity and access for non-human actors, including service accounts, delegated identity and role-based agent identity.
Experience evaluating non-deterministic systems, including test-set design, regression testing, quality gates and launch-readiness decisions.
Experience designing observability and cost controls for token-priced environments.
Experience designing controlled sandboxes or evaluation environments for emerging AI tools, with access controls, logging, data and intellectual-property restrictions and spend limits.
Security architecture literacy sufficient to be a credible counterpart to a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) organisation.
Ability to write a technical assessment that engineers and vendors cannot bluff past.
Experience setting standards for AI systems that take actions in enterprise systems, including authorization, approval, auditability and failure recovery.
Experience advising technical teams on the secure adoption of AI developer tools and specialist AI platforms.
Ability to act as the senior technical voice in the room, prototype critical paths when needed and deliver through engineering and business-unit teams.

Not Required

Model training or fine-tuning depth
Data platform or pipeline engineering experience
Owning ongoing feature delivery for business applications
Experience managing a large engineering organisation

Preferred Qualifications

Experience setting architecture standards, reference patterns or technical governance in a complex, matrixed organization.
Experience working across multiple business units or brands with different platforms, data boundaries and operating practices.
Experience in sports, media, entertainment, hospitality or live events, or with organizations managing large content libraries, talent data and fan-facing products.

Leadership Attributes

Opinionated and decisive:
makes the technical call, explains the tradeoffs and owns the recommendation.
Systems thinker:
designs durable patterns that work across platforms rather than solving one use case at a time.
Earned authority:
influences senior engineers, security leaders, vendors and business stakeholders without relying on direct reporting lines.
Low ego, high standards:
challenges weak technical reasoning while working constructively with partner teams.
Comfortable with ambiguity:
builds the architecture and operating standards as AI scales rather than waiting for a finished model.
Every AI portfolio decision has clear technical input on architecture, feasibility, effort, total cost and technical risk.

jobs.title: Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
Iterative Health is a healthcare technology and services company powering the acceleration of clinical research to transform patient outcomes.
We built a leading performance-driven network of 100+ sites across the US, Europe, India, and Australia, conducting research directly in the communities where care is delivered across gastrointestinal, hepatology, obesity, and cardiology. By combining deep clinical trial expertise with cutting-edge AI, we connect sponsors' scientific ambitions with high-performing research teams that expedite and expand access to novel therapeutics for patients in need. Today, Iterative Health is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and New York City with 250+ employees world-wide.

The Director, IT will lead Iterative Health’s technology infrastructure, systems, security, and IT operations as the company continues to scale across its corporate and clinical research network. This role will be responsible for building a secure, reliable, and scalable technology environment that enables employees to do their best work while supporting the operational needs of a growing healthcare technology and services organization.
The ideal candidate is a strategic and hands-on IT leader who can balance long-term technology planning with day-to-day execution. You will partner closely with leaders across teams to ensure technology solutions are aligned with business priorities, scalable, secure, and user-friendly.
Where You’ll Drive Impact IT Strategy & Leadership Develop and execute a scalable IT strategy aligned with Iterative Health’s business and growth objectives.
Establish IT roadmaps, priorities, standards, and operating processes across the organization.
Serve as a strategic technology advisor to executive and functional leaders.
Evaluate emerging technologies and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, and employee experience.
Develop and manage the IT budget, vendors, contracts, and technology investments.
Build and mature the IT function from an initial lean team into a scalable organization capable of supporting a rapidly growing, multi-site healthcare technology and services business.
Lead, coach, and develop the Corporate IT team.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, service expectations, and performance metrics.

Infrastructure & IT Operations Oversee corporate IT infrastructure, networks, endpoints, applications, identity management, and collaboration tools.
Ensure reliable, streamlined, secure, and scalable technology across corporate offices, remote employees, and clinical research sites while keeping costs efficient.
Establish standards for device provisioning, lifecycle management, access management, and technical support.
Build effective IT service management processes, including help desk, incident management, asset management, and service-level expectations.
Establish the IT operating model, organizational structure, processes, policies, and service standards required to support the company’s evolving technology needs.

Coordinate incident response and business continuity planning for technology-related risks and lead information and security for the company.

Support technology integrations related to acquisitions, partnerships, and organizational growth.

Establish standards for SSO, automated provisioning/deprovisioning, role-based access, and application access reviews.

Identify technology risks, integration costs, system redundancies, and remediation requirements during due diligence.
Develop transition plans for identity, endpoints, collaboration platforms, networking, SaaS applications, and security controls.

What You Bring 10+ years of progressive IT experience, including significant experience leading enterprise IT operations.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field preferred.
Experience leading IT within a high-growth, healthcare, technology, life sciences, or similarly complex organization.
Proven experience developing and executing an enterprise IT strategy and roadmap.
Strong understanding of infrastructure, SaaS applications, networking, endpoint management, identity and access management, and cybersecurity.
Experience managing IT budgets, vendors, technology implementations, and third-party service providers.
Experience building and leading high-performing IT teams.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and translate business needs into practical technology solutions.
Strong understanding of IT governance, security, privacy, compliance, and risk management.
Experience supporting distributed or multi-site organizations preferred.
Experience with M&A technology integration or organizational scaling strongly preferred.
Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.

Comfortable navigating evolving business priorities and opportunities

Job Description

Our Data Streaming Platform team is seeking a Sr. Engineering Manager to support our data streaming platform (ownership of real-time data pipelines and streaming infrastructure built on Kafka, Temporal, and Airflow). Qualified candidates must be able to help foster an inspiring workplace where talented people feel empowered to drive operational excellence, mature compliance practices, and business results. As a Sr. Engineering Manager for the platform team, you will report to the Sr. Director of Engineering and lead a distributed team of software engineers. In partnership with technical program management, you will define processes and measurements to ensure strength in performance and delivery. You will own technical solutions—in accordance with Nordstrom’s engineering standards—and you will be accountable for recruiting and hiring talent as well as coaching and mentoring your team members in their career.

You are a highly technical leader with a bias towards action and the ability to drive consensus. You are comfortable discussing software architecture and leveraging data to influence decisions. You have a proven understanding of the fundamentals of agile processes, deep knowledge of software development lifecycle and an experience to draw from that helps you build towards a future state while making smart tradeoffs to meet current objectives. You are a creative problem solver, and you know how to measure and improve your products and teams.

The Data Streaming Platform team enables real-time data movement and event-driven infrastructure that powers our company’s strategic objectives. To support these activities, we must also focus on providing a secure, scalable, and highly available streaming infrastructure and operational environment.

This role is offered as hybrid in Seattle, WA. Candidates must be available to work in office at the Nordstrom corporate headquarters a minimum of 4 days/week to be considered for this position.

A day in the life…

End to end ownership of cross-functional projects, including product definition, roadmap planning, resource planning and project execution
Driving the roadmap and vision for the teams, collaborate with product groups and partner teams to deliver value to our customers

At the heart of this role is delivery. You will be hands-on in driving the delivery of critical business initiatives, managing all aspects of the project such as project planning, budget tracking, requirements definition, risk management, communication, and implementation planning

A BA/BS in Computer Science or closely related degree or equivalent practical experience

Technology background, especially in cloud-based, event-driven architecture with a deep understanding of distributed systems and streaming data pipelines, and a passion for data and analytics

Experience working with cloud technologies, manage scalable solutions that are truly full-stack: frontend, backend, data engineering, DB, dev-ops, CI/CD, support

jobs.description:
About Us:

We are an innovative AdTech company focused on Artificial Intelligence and SaaS. We are dedicated to reshaping industry efficiency and user experience through cutting-edge AI technology. Our products already serve a wide range of enterprise clients, and we are in a rapid growth phase where technology is our core competitive advantage. We are now seeking a visionary and experienced Chief Technology Officer to lead our technical team, deeply integrate AI capabilities into our SaaS products, and help build an industry-defining platform.

Key Responsibilities:

- Fully own the company’s technology strategy and execution; define the technical roadmap for AI and SaaS products to ensure strong alignment between technology direction and business objectives.
- Lead and build a high-performing technical organization covering AI algorithms, engineering, architecture, data, and related domains; continuously improve team capability and delivery efficiency.
- Drive the design, optimization, and large-scale implementation of core AI capabilities (large language model applications, machine learning, recommendation systems, intelligent decision-making, etc.) together with the overall SaaS platform architecture.
- Architect highly available, high-concurrency, and scalable systems to ensure product stability and performance under rapid growth.

Responsibilities

MaxLinear is seeking a Director of Product Engineering to join our team. In this role, you will focus on the following:

Build and mentor engineering talent while fostering a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and innovation
Drive seamless transition of products from design to manufacturing and own product manufacturing performance throughout the entire product lifecycle
Lead product bring-up, silicon validation, characterization, qualification, and production release activities
Define organizational strategy, goals, KPIs, and resource plans aligned with company objectives
Collaborate closely with cross functional organizations to optimize performance, yield, testability, and manufacturability
Establish manufacturing readiness criteria and ensure successful product ramp

Analyze product and test data to identify yield detractors and implement corrective actions
Develop strategies to improve cost of test, manufacturing efficiency, and overall product margins
Support customer escalations, product quality investigations, and field-return analysis
Establish and manage OSAT scorecards and KPIs to ensure world-class execution in quality, yield, cost, delivery, and cycle time

Qualifications

Experience with releasing products on advanced CMOS Process nodes (16nm and below)
Deep knowledge of mm-wave, RF, Mixed signal and CMOS logic circuit principles
Knowledge and experience with ATE (Automatic Test Equipment), such as Verigy and Teradyne
Experience with Data Analysis S/W such as Galaxy, Data Conductor or DataPower to create Characterization Reports and monitor production Yield
Experience recruiting, managing, and mentoring an engineering team
BS in Electrical Engineering or related + 13 years of experience, or MS + 11 years of experience, or Ph.D. + 8 years of experience

Compensation And Benefits

MaxLinear has a Total Compensation philosophy which includes base salary and annual discretionary bonus eligibility and many positions also include stock-based compensation.

MaxLinear's good faith estimate starting base salary range is: $ 187,000 to $251 , Annually

We offer competitive benefits designed to support employee health, welfare, and retirement and some highlights are: health care benefits, 401k savings plan, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), and paid time off.

The actual starting base salary will be determined by the match to certain role-related criteria such as educational degree(s) or equivalent, relevant work experience, skillset needed for the role, and geographic location; this is not an all-inclusive list as some roles may require unique skills or experience.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, and will not be discriminated against based on race, sex, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status.

Company Overview

MaxLinear is a global, NASDAQ-traded company (MXL) where the entrepreneurial spirit is alive and well. We are a fabless system-on-chip product company, striving to improve the world’s communication networks for everyone through our highly integrated radio-frequency (RF), analog, digital, and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions for access and connectivity, wired and wireless infrastructure, and industrial and multi-market applications.

We hire the best people in the industry and engage them in some of the most exciting opportunities that connect the world we live in today. Our growth has come from innovative, bold approaches to solving some of the world’s most challenging communication technology problems in the most efficient and effective manner.

MaxLinear began by developing the world’s first high-performance TV tuner chip using standard CMOS process technology. Others said we couldn’t achieve the extremely high-performance requirements using CMOS, but we proved them wrong and achieved enduring global market leadership with our designs. Since then, we’ve developed a full line of products that drive 4G and 5G infrastructure; enable data center, metro and long-haul optical interconnects; bring 10Gbit to the home; power the IoT revolution; and enable robust and reliable communication in harsh industrial environments. Over the years, we’ve expanded through organic growth and through several acquisitions that have perfectly complemented our existing portfolio and enabled us to deliver complete end-to-end solutions in our target markets. One such example was the acquisition of Intel’s Home Gateway Platform Division that added Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and Broadband Gateway Processor SoC technology to our connected home portfolio creating a complete and scalable platform of connectivity and access solutions to fully address our customers’ needs.

Our headquarters are in Carlsbad, near San Diego, California. We also have major design centers in Irvine and San Jose, California; Valencia, Spain; Bangalore, India; Munich, Germany; Israel; and Singapore.

We have approximately 1,200 employees, a substantial majority of whom have engineering degrees and include masters and Ph.D. graduates from many of the premiere universities around the world. Our employees thrive on innovation, outstanding execution, outside-the-box thinking, nimbleness, and collaboration. Together, we form a high-energy business team that is focused on building the best and most innovative products on the market.

From delivering affordable broadband to protecting against cybersecurity threats and building digital government services, OTI is at the forefront of how the city delivers for New Yorkers in the 21st century. Follow us on social media @NYCOfficeofTech, and visit www.nyc.gov/oti to learn more.

At OTI, we offer great benefits, and the chance to work on projects that have a meaningful impact on millions of people. You'll have the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology and collaborate with other passionate professionals who share your drive and commitment to making a difference through technology.

OUR WORK

The Public Interest Technology (PIT) Crew, at the NYC Office of Technology and Innovation, builds the technology, products, and services needed to deliver a more affordable New York City. We design, build, and launch exceptional public-facing products for New Yorkers.

Job Description

We are hiring a PIT Crew Executive Director of Engineering to build and shape the direction of the PIT Crew. This is a hands-on executive director position. You will work to drive clarity and action in ambiguity; pair closely with designers, engineers, product managers, user researchers, policy experts, and other city employees to help the team move from problem statements to working products and services for New Yorkers; define and lead the software engineering practice for the PIT Crew and enable the team to do exceptional engineering work; serve as an expert in your craft; and be comfortable diving into unblock work, however the situation demands - including individual contributor work. In addition to enabling a suite of short-term projects, you will help determine PIT Crew’s long-term direction; synthesize strategy with an eye towards building long-term momentum; advise on team structure and hiring practices; and build a culture of delivering rapidly and responsibly for New Yorkers.

Responsibilities will include:

Build and lead a high-performing team focused on delivering measurable impact for New Yorkers.
Establish modern best practices for your discipline and promote adoption.
Manage and mentor talent effectively to ensure their time serving the City of New York is positive and meaningful.
Foster a culture of speed, quality, pragmatism, and public service.
Own and drive the team’s high-level roadmap. Identify and scope new projects. Manage project allocation and staffing.
Ensure product launches are successful and deliver measurable impact for New Yorkers. Ensure all delivered products meet high standards of usability, accessibility, security and privacy.
Collaborate and drive alignment across a wide range of stakeholders, including within the Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI), City Hall, other City agencies, and external partners;
Oversee special projects and initiatives as assigned.

HOURS/SHIFT

Day - Due to the necessary management duties of this position in a 24/7 operation, candidate may be required to be on call and/or work various shifts such as weekends and/or nights/evenings.

WORK LOCATION

Brooklyn, NY

TO APPLY

Please go to www.cityjobs.nyc.gov and search for Job ID #803565

Interested applicants with other civil service titles who meet the preferred requirements should also submit a resume for consideration

SUBMISSION OF A RESUME IS NOT A GUARANTEE THAT YOU WILL RECEIVE AN INTERVIEW

APPOINTMENTS ARE SUBJECT TO OVERSIGHT APPROVAL

OTI participates in E-Verify

EXECUTIVE PROGRAM SPECIALIST - 06940

Minimum Qualifications

A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and five years of satisfactory full-time experience related to projects and policies required by the particular position;

or

Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" above.

Preferred Skills

The successful candidate should possess the following skills and experience: - 10+ years of experience building consumer technology, including hands-on experience shipping products in complex, regulated or legacy environments where the constraints are challenging and the data is imperfect. - Experience designing, hiring and composing high-performance teams. - Experience managing and mentoring engineering teams across disciplines and skill levels. - Comfort with ambiguity. Ability to dive into an undefined problem space and shape a long-term strategy. - Best-in-class attention to detail with strong written and verbal communication skills - Communicate upwards with clarity. Represent the team effectively with cross-functional and executive stakeholders.

As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal loan forgiveness programs and state repayment assistance programs. For more information, please visit the U.S. Department of Education’s website at https://studentaid.gov/pslf/.

To determine if the residency requirement applies to you, please discuss with the agency representative at the time of interview.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Context and Semantics Engineering (AI)
new_jobs.description:
Your work days are brighter here.

We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.

About The Team

The Data Cloud organization is at the forefront of Workday’s next major wave of innovation, driven by a bold mandate to build the industry’s first true Platform for Agents. We are a high-energy, ambitious team that balances Workday's deep foundational expertise with fresh, forward-thinking perspectives to accelerate our pace of delivery and unlock massive new commercial value. By leveraging Workday’s unique business context, trusted data, and identity guardrails, we are building the critical engine that will power the future of AI and agentic workflows across the enterprise. As a team, we value organizational clarity, deep cross-functional collaboration, and rapid execution, working together to evolve our architecture and aggressively scale our impact in the market.

Join the Data Cloud organization, where we are building the intelligent foundation for Workday's next generation of AI Agents. The Context and Semantics Engineering team is the brain trust responsible for making our AI "enterprise-aware." We build the semantic layers, knowledge graphs, and dynamic context engines that ground generative AI in real-world HR and Finance data. By bridging the gap between raw enterprise data and large language models (LLMs), our team ensures that Workday’s autonomous agents can reason accurately, securely, and with deep contextual awareness at a global scale.

About The Role

As the Senior Director of Context and Semantics Engineering, you will be a key engineering executive driving the vision, architecture, and delivery of the intelligence layer powering Workday’s AI Agents. You will lead and scale an engineering organization to build highly scalable semantic engines, advanced RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines, vector search infrastructure, and dynamic context-management systems.

Sitting at the critical intersection of data architecture and applied AI, you will ensure that our foundational models seamlessly understand and reason over complex, highly regulated enterprise workflows. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role requiring a visionary leader who can scale organizations, navigate technical ambiguity, and deliver production-grade AI infrastructure that sets the industry standard for Enterprise AI.

Responsibilities:

Organizational Leadership: Build, scale, and mentor a world-class engineering organization dedicated to AI context, semantic architecture, and data orchestration.
Strategic Technical Vision: Define and execute the technical roadmap for Workday’s AI semantic layer, encompassing vector databases, knowledge graphs, enterprise ontologies, and semantic search capabilities.
AI & RAG Infrastructure: Lead the development of enterprise-grade RAG pipelines, ensuring LLMs are grounded in real-time, accurate, and tenant-isolated HR and Finance data to eliminate hallucinations and drive agentic reasoning.
Cross-Functional Executive Partnership: Collaborate tightly with VP/C-level stakeholders across AI/ML Engineering, Product Management, and Platform Architecture to seamlessly integrate context engines into the broader AI Agent Factory and Sana experiences.
Context & Memory Management: Drive the engineering design for agentic memory, state management, and conversational context, allowing our AI agents to seamlessly handle multi-turn, complex user workflows.
Responsible & Governed AI: Enforce rigorous technical standards for data privacy, RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), and compliance, ensuring that context fed to AI models strictly adheres to enterprise security boundaries.
Innovation & Scale: Evaluate and integrate cutting-edge AI data technologies and orchestration frameworks (e.g., advanced embedding models, GraphRAG, LlamaIndex, LangChain) to future-proof Workday's AI platform at massive scale.

About You

Basic Qualifications:

10+ years of progressive software engineering experience with a strong background in distributed systems, search architectures, data platforms, or AI infrastructure.
5+ years of senior engineering leadership experience (Director level or above), with a proven track record of managing managers, scaling organizations (50+ engineers), and delivering mission-critical enterprise systems.
3+ years of direct experience leading teams that build AI/ML infrastructure, semantic search engines, LLM orchestration layers, vector databases, or Knowledge Graphs.

Other Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field (Ph.D. is a plus).
Deep architectural understanding of how to bridge structured enterprise data with unstructured AI models (RAG architectures, embedding generation, chunking strategies, and semantic routing).
Experience building and scaling Semantic Layers, Ontologies, or enterprise-scale Search/Retrieval systems (e.g., Elasticsearch, Pinecone, Milvus, Neo4j).
Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex AI and data concepts into clear business value for non-technical stakeholders.
Product-first mindset with a relentless focus on delivering high-reliability, low-latency infrastructure that powers real-time AI user experiences.
Experience operating within highly regulated data environments (Finance/HR) and implementing AI guardrails for enterprise-grade security.
Experience with the Workday platform and architecture is a strong plus.

Workday Pay Transparency Statement

The annualized base salary ranges for the primary location and any additional locations are listed below. Workday pay ranges vary based on work location. As a part of the total compensation package, this role may be eligible for the Workday Bonus Plan or a role-specific commission/bonus, as well as annual refresh stock grants. Recruiters can share more detail during the hiring process. Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, skills, job duties, and business need, among other things. For more information regarding Workday’s comprehensive benefits, please click here.

Primary Location: USA.CA.Pleasanton

Primary Location Base Pay Range: $281,600 USD - $422,400 USD

Additional US Location(s) Base Pay Range: $231,800 USD - $422,400 USD

Our Approach to Flexible Work

With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. We know that flexibility can take shape in many ways, so rather than a number of required days in-office each week, we simply spend at least half (50%) of our time each quarter in the office or in the field
with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter.

Unusual Machines is a U.S.-based drone and drone parts company focused on the small and First-Person View (FPV) segments of the drone market. Our brands - Rotor Riot, Fat Shark, Rotor Lab and - coming soon - Upgrade Energy - are some of the most respected names in FPV and have helped shape the industry through e-commerce, product development, and a deep connection with the pilot community.

We’re expanding into enterprise and defense - bringing our obsessive attention to performance, design, and U.S.-based manufacturing into high-stakes environments like search and rescue and military innovation. With several of our products already approved by the Defense Innovation Unit, we’re solving procurement issues for customers who demand speed, agility, and compliance.

If you love working at the intersection of community, content, and cutting-edge technology, you’ll feel right at home here.

Director of Process Engineering

You in this Role
You are a disciplined engineering leader who excels at scaling manufacturing processes and building world-class teams. Joining our site in Orlando, FL, you will step into a vital leadership role at an exciting point in our growth. With a large, dedicated production team focused on high-touch assembly, your mission is to introduce the advanced engineering rigor needed to take our operations to the next level. You will focus on standardizing workflows, establishing data-driven habits, and mentoring our engineering team to help them grow professionally.

In this onsite role, you will directly manage Process Engineering Managers in Motors/Flex and Cameras/Headsets/Batteries.

What You'll Do

Develop the Team: Serve as a coach and mentor to the process engineering team, fostering professional growth and building a strong culture of technical excellence.
Establish Engineering Rigor: Introduce and standardize structured engineering workflows, bringing operational discipline to our assembly environment.
Drive Quality with Data: Implement Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Six Sigma methodologies to optimize manual assembly processes and minimize variance.
Own Traceability & Systems: Maximize the utilization of our Manufacturing Execution System (MES), ensure robust component traceability, and maintain strict document control.
Lead Continuous Improvement: Utilize DMAIC and Lean tools to identify assembly bottlenecks, improve production yields, and eliminate waste.
Empower Leadership: Guide and support your two engineering managers, aligning their teams' goals with the company's scaling milestones.

What You'll Bring

Industry Expertise: A proven background in semiconductor or microelectronics manufacturing, where strict process control and high-quality standards are second nature.
Passion for Mentorship: A strong desire to teach, coach, and elevate engineers at various stages of their career development.
Methodology Expertise: Deep knowledge of Six Sigma, DMAIC, SPC, and Continuous Improvement framework (Six Sigma Black Belt is highly desirable).
System Proficiency: Strong familiarity with MES platforms, product traceability protocols, and formal document control workflows.
Proven Leadership: Experience successfully managing other engineering managers or leading high-performing technical teams in an onsite manufacturing environment.
Component Familiarity: Experience or familiarity with hardware components like motors, flex circuits, camera modules, or battery packs is a plus.
Education & Experience: A Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline is preferred, combined with a strong track record of bringing structure and stability to growing production lines.

Compensation - $130,000 - 170,000

new_jobs.title: Director of Agent Deployment Engineering
new_jobs.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.

About The Team

Over the past few years, development of LLMs has evolved at a rapid pace. It’s not enough for our customers to just “set it and forget it” when it comes to AI software. Truly successful AI Agents require hands-on execution, rigorous iteration, and deep technical delivery to reach enterprise-grade performance.

We’re creating an Agent Deployment Engineering Org
: a specialized technical delivery team responsible for end-to-end execution of AI agent builds. Agent Deployment Engineers own the hands-on work required to deliver best-in-class agents—writing and configuring key components, validating integrations, and ensuring agents perform reliably at scale. This team brings greater specialization and focus to build quality. Agent Deployment Engineers are technical and customer-facing: interfacing with senior technical stakeholders while going deep on agent configuration and build execution.

About The Role

As Director of Agent Deployment Engineering
, you will lead Decagon’s technical delivery for strategic enterprise customers—owning outcomes across multiple deployments and building the team, playbooks, and operating system required to scale. This is a senior, customer-facing leadership role where you’ll partner with customer executives and technical leaders to define success, translate requirements into delivery plans, and drive launches that measurably impact customer outcomes.

You’ll work closely with Agent PMs, Agent Success, Engineering, and GTM leadership to create tight feedback loops: driving delivery, surfacing product gaps, and influencing the evolution of Decagon’s agent-building platform based on real enterprise needs. This role is ideal for a leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, enjoys shipping customer-facing technical work, and can balance hands-on problem solving with structured execution at scale.

In this role, you will

Lead and scale a high-performing delivery org
Own end-to-end execution of AI agent deployments for enterprise customers across a portfolio, from scoping through launch and iteration.
Build, lead, and develop a team of Agent Builders; hire, coach, and set a high bar for quality, velocity, and customer outcomes.
Establish delivery operating rhythms (planning, reviews, retros), capacity planning, and forecasting to ensure predictable execution.

Drive executive-level customer engagements
Interface with senior technical stakeholders and executives to define success criteria, align on constraints (security/compliance), and drive delivery against timelines.
Lead complex escalations and unblock cross-functional teams when quality, timelines, or customer outcomes are at risk.
Translate customer needs into crisp internal documentation and execution plans across Product/Engineering/GTM.

Create repeatable playbooks and scale mechanisms
Define and standardize delivery methodologies and artifacts (e.g., AOP quality bar, launch readiness checklists, iteration loops).
Establish best practices for evaluation and guardrails to ensure safe, compliant, and predictable agent performance in real-world scenarios.
Improve tooling and processes to reduce time-to-launch and increase reliability across deployments.

Influence the platform roadmap through deployment insights
Identify recurring product/platform gaps and drive prioritization with Engineering and Product leadership.
Partner with internal teams to turn real customer needs into platform improvements that compound across deployments.

Your background looks something like this

10+ years of relevant experience in technical, customer-facing roles (e.g., forward-deployed engineering, solutions engineering, technical consulting, implementation engineering, technical product/PM, or similar).
5+ years of people management experience, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and building high-performing teams; ideally experience leading senior ICs and/or managers.
Strong technical foundation—comfortable working with APIs, integrations, and complex systems; able to go deep to diagnose issues and guide solution architecture.
Experience delivering production-grade customer solutions that require structured execution, testing/validation, and iteration.
Ability to communicate clearly with senior technical stakeholders, translate requirements into execution plans, and drive delivery.
Comfort operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where you build structure while maintaining momentum.

Even better if you have

Experience deploying LLM-based products or AI agents in production (prompting, evaluation, guardrails, tooling, workflow design).
Experience with enterprise SaaS integrations (e.g., ticketing systems, CRM, data pipelines) and security/compliance considerations.
Strong product instincts—ability to define success metrics, write crisp requirements, and contribute customer insight back into product roadmap.
Experience scaling a delivery function from high-touch execution to repeatable playbooks and durable operating cadence.

Job Description

General Summary:

This role leads a team responsible for the architecture, delivery, security, support, and continuous evolution of enterprise laboratory technology platforms across LC1/2, Vertex's Cell & Gene Therapy (CGT) site. It is also the single accountable Research Site Partner for LC1/2: the primary DTE relationship holder for the site leadership, and the front door through which site requirements are captured, shaped, and routed into the correct cross-functional platform backlog.

Operating within highly regulated GxP and SOX environments, this role remains accountable for operational excellence, financial stewardship, and risk management across a complex laboratory technology landscape, including ownership of the site's annual operating budget. In parallel, the role carries accountability for local technology adoption, change management, and cross-site prioritization advocacy — ensuring LC1/2's voice shapes the shared platform roadmap without the site building or maintaining local one-off solutions.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

Technology & Operations Leadership

Build and sustain strong, trust-based relationships with senior business, quality, and DTE leaders, acting as a strategic partner with sustained impact on enterprise laboratory goals.

new_jobs.description:
About Fora

Fora is the modern travel agency
, empowering anyone with a passion for travel to build a thriving advisory business. We're modernizing the $100B+ travel agency industry by combining powerful technology, data, and community to enable thousands of entrepreneurs to build on our platform. Our business-in-a-box platform
gives travel entrepreneurs everything they need to launch and scale, from cutting-edge tools and personalized training to a vibrant community
and exclusive industry partnerships. At the heart of it all is our mission: to help the next generation of travel entrepreneurs turn their love for travel into a fulfilling career
, whether full-time or part-time. We believe that everyone, from seasoned professionals to first-time advisors, can build something both profitable and personal.

Founded in 2021 by seasoned entrepreneurs, Fora has grown steadily since, expanding to a team of 200+ full-time employees
based in downtown New York City
. In 2026,
we announced our $60 million Series D investment round
, led by Forerunner and Tactile Ventures, with continued participation from existing investors Thrive Capital, Insight Partners, and Heartcore Capital. We've also been recognized as a LinkedIn Top Startup 2024, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies 2025 and 2023, and we were most recently recognized as one of the TIME100 Most Influential Companies 2026.

We're building the first truly unified platform for all travel needs—leveraging the best of human expertise and technology to transform how people plan and book travel.

About The Role

Fora is looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead and empower several cross-functional sprint teams on Fora’s Finance pod. Our pod’s mission is to build the financial operating system for a new generation of travel entrepreneurs, owning the complete lifecycle from ingesting bookings and collecting commissions from suppliers to giving advisors transparency into their earnings and paying them quickly, accurately, and seamlessly. You’ll collaborate closely with Product, Design, Operations, and your engineering teams to set strategy, steer architecture, and drive impactful business outcomes across multiple teams. Our rails processed commission payments on over $1B in travel last year, so your work will involve figuring out how to move fast and stay nimble while operating on a system where pivot costs are high, errors lose money, and downtime is not an option.

We expect our managers to be masters of the craft and be able to go deep into the details, mastering the fundamentals and honing their skills. The ideal candidate is a first principles thinker who is passionate about developing people, driving technical excellence, and achieving sustainable business results through thoughtful leadership and collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

Collaborate with Product and Design to shape product strategy, ensuring that your team builds the right solutions that drive the highest impact on the business.
Improve team efficiency and engineering velocity, ensuring your team delivers value quickly without compromising on quality, maintainability, or reliability.
Guide architecture and technical decisions, balancing trade-offs and proactively anticipating future issues to ensure robust and scalable solutions.
Drive operational excellence across reliability, performance, cost-efficiency, design consistency, and maintainable code.
Promote high team engagement, employee happiness, continuous skill development, and professional growth.
Mentor engineers, provide constructive feedback, and support direct reports to help them overcome challenges and deliver on ambitious goals.
Perform hands-on technical work, contributing to code reviews, debugging, and implementing functionality.
Participate in hiring processes and attracting top engineering talent to support the continued growth of your team and our organization.

Requirements

4+ years of experience in engineering leadership roles (e.g., Engineering Manager or Tech Lead) in the consumer-facing fintech space, including 1+ years of experience managing managers.
8+ years experience in web systems development.
Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers, effectively manage performance, and build highly motivated, engaged teams.
Strong technical acumen, with experience making informed architectural decisions, addressing technical debt, and setting robust engineering standards.
Exceptional project management and organizational skills, including the ability to break down complex projects, anticipate risks, and deliver consistently high-quality outcomes.
Excellent communication skills, able to translate technical concepts clearly to diverse stakeholders and facilitate productive, drama-free project launches.
Proven recruiting experience, capable of evaluating engineering candidates effectively and representing the company positively.
A collaborative, empathetic leadership style that emphasizes humility, openness to feedback, accountability, and continuous learning.
Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort working in an early- to mid-stage startup environment where ambiguity and pace are part of the fun.
First-principles thinker who carefully evaluates each problem, thoughtfully choosing between established best practices and bespoke solutions, especially when designing team processes and norms.

Compensation

Compensation range for this role can vary depending on experience, and for this role an indicative range is $235k-$250k + equity. Other benefits include:

Unlimited vacation
Health Insurance (including an option completely covered by Fora HQ)
Dental & Vision Insurance
Wellhub Memberships
401k plan with company match
Commuter Benefits
Supplemental Life Insurance
Stock Options

This role is based in our beautiful New York City office (Tribeca/Fidi) with lots of natural light and great views.

Our Values

We’re forging our own path

Fora has always been about driving change within the industry. We’re not interested in maintaining the status quo.

We’re stronger together

Community is our cornerstone and collective power is our strength. We believe we can all go further when we operate together, using our combined leverage to unlock better opportunities and outcomes for our advisors, partners, and travelers.

We believe in technology

We believe technology is an answer to some of the most fundamental challenges the travel industry faces. We believe advancements in AI, bold investments in our platforms, and a world-class data infrastructure will transform the work of our advisors and our partners, while creating better travel experiences for travelers.

We’re here to serve

We operate in service of our community and believe that when they’re empowered to focus on what they do best, we all win. It’s why we relentlessly advocate for our advisors and prioritize their best interest every step of the way.

We mean business

Fora is equal parts fun, meaningful work and serious travel business. We’re unlocking opportunities for thousands of travel entrepreneurs, delivering a stream of high-quality guests at scale for our partners, and providing a superior travel experience for our travelers. It’s a better equation for the future of our industry.

WORK AUTHORIZATION

Authorization to work in the United States is required for full-time roles based in our New York City office. Fora is unable to sponsor or assist with U.S. work authorization. Roles based outside of the United States are not subject to this requirement.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

new_jobs.description:
Job Family

About Us

At Transamerica, hard work, innovative thinking, and personal accountability are qualities we honor and reward. We understand the potential of leveraging the talents of a diverse workforce. We embrace an environment where employees enjoy a balance between their careers, families, communities, and personal interests.

Ultimately, we appreciate the uniqueness of a company where talented professionals work collaboratively in a positive environment — one focused on helping people look forward and plan for the best life possible while providing tools and solutions that make it easier to get there.

Who We Are

We believe everyone deserves to live their best life. More than a century ago, we were among the first financial services companies in America to serve everyday people from all walks of life.

Today, we’re part of an international holding company, with millions of customers and thousands of employees worldwide. Our insurance, retirement, and investment solutions help people make the most of what’s important to them.

We’re empowered by a vast agent network covering North America, with diversity to match. Together with our nonprofit research institute and foundation, we tune in, step up, and are a force for good — for our customers and the communities where we live, work, and play. United in our purpose, we help people create the financial freedom to live life on their terms.

What We Do

Transamerica is organized into three distinct businesses. These include 1) World Financial Group, including Transamerica Financial Advisors, 2) Protection Solutions and Savings & Investments, comprised of life insurance, annuities, employee benefits, retirement plans, and Transamerica Investment Solutions, and 3) Financial Assets, which includes legacy blocks of long term care, universal life, and variable and fixed annuities. These are supported by Transamerica Corporate, which includes Finance, People and Places, General Counsel, Risk, Internal Audit, Strategy and Development, and Corporate Affairs, which covers Communications, Brand, and Government and Policy Affairs.

Transamerica employs nearly 7,000 people. It’s part of Aegon, an integrated, diversified, international financial services group serving approximately 23.9 million customers worldwide.* For more information, visit transamerica.com. 

Job Description Summary

We are seeking a strategic and experienced Procurement Technology leader with a Financial Services / Insurance background to lead the global technology platforms, integrations, data capabilities, and engineering teams that support enterprise procurement. This role is responsible for enabling efficient, compliant, and scalable source-to-pay, procure-to-pay, supplier management, contract management, purchasing, invoice, and spend analytics capabilities across a global insurance organization, Aegon / Transamerica.

The leader will partner closely with Global Procurement, Finance, Enterprise Architecture, Security, Data Governance, and regional Procurement business stakeholders to modernize procurement technology, improve operational resilience, strengthen controls, optimize vendor and SaaS ecosystems, and advance automation and AI-enabled procurement capabilities.

Responsibilities

Job Description

Leadership, Technical Strategy & Innovation

Build and maintain a forward-looking global Procurement Technology strategy and roadmap aligned to business priorities, procurement operating model needs, enterprise architecture standards, regulatory obligations, and regional execution requirements.
Serve as the technology owner and strategic partner for procurement platforms and capabilities, including source-to-contract, procure-to-pay, supplier lifecycle management, contract lifecycle management, purchasing, invoice automation, vendor master, spend analytics, supplier risk, and procurement reporting.
Evaluate, rationalize, modernize, and integrate procurement technology solutions across global and local environments, balancing business agility, operational risk, total cost of ownership, security, data quality, and enterprise standardization.
Identify and implement opportunities to leverage cloud-native platforms, SaaS platforms, API-led integration, automation, workflow orchestration, data management, analytics, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and Generative AI to improve procurement productivity, policy compliance, exception management, supplier insight, and decision support.
Partner with enterprise architecture, information security, data governance, risk, and procurement leadership to ensure procurement solutions comply with internal standards, privacy requirements, third-party risk expectations, audit controls, and regional regulatory requirements.
Establish clear technology guardrails and design patterns for procurement solutions, integrations, reporting, data flows, user access, and support models across global and regional teams.

Team Management

Lead, mentor, and grow a geographically distributed team of software engineers, platform owners, analysts, and external delivery partners supporting procurement technology globally.
Foster a culture of inclusion, accountability, engineering excellence, operational ownership, continuous improvement, and customer-focused delivery.
Partner with Global Procurement, Finance, Legal, Risk, Compliance, and regional technology teams to align priorities, manage demand, resolve conflicts, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
Build the team’s capability across procurement processes, financial services controls, SaaS platform management, integration patterns, data quality, cloud engineering, automation, and production support.
Manage resource capacity, budget, vendor performance, delivery plans, and support coverage across multiple geographies and time zones.

Technology Execution

Oversee the design, implementation, integration, maintenance, and modernization of global procurement technology platforms and related enterprise integrations.
Drive reliable end-to-end procurement technology delivery across source-to-pay and procure-to-pay processes, including requisitioning, approvals, purchase orders, supplier onboarding, contract data, invoice processing, payment handoffs, vendor risk workflows, reporting, and analytics.
Ensure procurement systems are scalable, secure, resilient, supportable, and compliant with financial services / insurance control expectations, including audit readiness, segregation of duties, data protection, records retention, and third-party risk management requirements.
Champion modern engineering practices, including DevOps, CI/CD, automated testing, observability, secure development, release management, incident management, batch/API reliability, and documentation.
Improve procurement data quality and governance across supplier, contract, spend, and performance data domains.
Lead technology input into procurement transformation efforts, SaaS platform upgrades, ERP integrations, finance transformation initiatives, operating model changes, and global standardization efforts.
Partner with enterprise data, finance, and procurement analytics teams to strengthen spend visibility, contract compliance reporting, supplier performance insight, category analytics, and executive-level procurement dashboards.
Ensure production stability through clear ownership, support models, service level expectations, monitoring, problem management, and root cause analysis for critical procurement processes.

Other Responsibilities

Provide technical guidance and leadership to development, platform, and support teams to deliver high-quality procurement solutions used by multiple business units, regions, and shared service functions.
Partner with senior leadership and stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Translate strategic priorities into defined roadmaps, tactical action plans, milestones, measurable outcomes, and execution governance.
Act as a strategist and champion for enterprise architecture, data governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience, and design principles as they apply to procurement technology.
Participate in whiteboard discussions, roadmap reviews, steering committees, architecture forums, vendor reviews, and executive presentations.
Act quickly and appropriately to solve problems, bring clarity, remove delivery impediments, and minimize business impact from incidents, defects, platform constraints, and unforeseen circumstances.
Drive a culture of change, excellence, prudent experimentation, and innovation that constructively challenges the status quo while maintaining strong risk, control, and production stability discipline.
Manage budget, expenditures, vendor performance, licensing, contracts, renewals, and technology investment tradeoffs in partnership with Procurement, Finance, and Technology leadership.
Support audit, regulatory, risk, and compliance activities by ensuring accurate documentation, evidence, control execution, remediation tracking, and technology ownership across procurement systems.

new_jobs.title: Senior Software Engineering Manager, Core OS — Vehicle Compute
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The Role

The Vehicle Experiences Engine (VEE) at GM is transforming how millions of people interact with their vehicles. At the foundation of that transformation is the Core OS group
— the team that builds the high-performance operating-system foundation on which GM's next generation of vehicle software runs. Our work spans hypervisors and virtualization, safety and health management, containerization, and the core OS services that let multiple operating systems — Linux, Android, and QNX — share a single high-compute platform safely and efficiently.

As Senior Software Engineering Manager, Core OS, you will build this team from the ground up. You'll define the charter, hire the founding engineers, set the architecture, and establish how the Core OS layer interfaces with the silicon, guest OS, and vehicle program teams around it. You will be accountable for both standing up the team and delivering its first production milestones.

This is a defining opportunity to shape the future of software-defined mobility: the platform your organization builds determines the computing efficiency, responsiveness, scalability, reliability of every experience layered on top of it, and across every vehicle program that ships on it — and makes GM's vehicles smarter, safer, and continuously upgradeable.

What You’ll Do:

Lead and grow a high-performing engineering organization of senior engineers and engineering leaders, fostering technical excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Own the roadmap and delivery of the core OS layer: hypervisor and virtualization, virtual machine lifecycle and resource partitioning, inter-VM communication, and the boot and secure-boot chain.
Deliver the safety-relevant foundation of the compute platform — freedom from interference between partitions, health monitoring, fault detection, and recovery — in partnership with functional safety and cybersecurity teams.
Establish on-vehicle container and workload management, including runtime isolation, lifecycle management, resource governance, and updateability of platform workloads.
Enable multiple guest operating systems — embedded Linux (Yocto), Android, and QNX — on shared compute, with consistent platform services, interfaces, and tooling across all of them.
Set and drive platform KPIs for compute efficiency, responsiveness, startup and boot time, memory footprint, scalability, and reliability.
Drive cross-functional collaboration with BSP and silicon enablement, application platform, cybersecurity, functional safety, and vehicle program teams to ensure seamless integration.
Build strong vendor and ecosystem partnerships — including silicon, RTOS, and hypervisor suppliers — and engage with relevant open-source and industry communities.
Ensure program execution excellence by tracking progress against vehicle milestones, managing risk, and partnering closely with program management.

Your Skills And Abilities (Required Qualifications)

10+ years of professional experience building embedded or systems software, with a strong foundation in operating system internals, virtualization, or real-time systems.
5+ years of engineering leadership experience, including leading senior engineers and managers, with a proven record of scaling teams and delivering results.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or related fields.
Demonstrated success delivering production-grade OS or platform software on modern SoC-based or embedded systems.
Demonstrated effectiveness in ambiguous, early-stage environments — defining scope, establishing interfaces with adjacent organizations, and making architectural commitments with incomplete information
Depth in at least one of: type-1 hypervisors and virtualization, real-time operating systems, or embedded Linux deployed at scale.
Proven ability to drive large-scale software programs to completion, including milestone planning, risk management, and cross-team coordination.
Strong technical credibility paired with the ability to set vision, influence architecture, and drive execution across multiple teams.
Demonstrated excellence in cross-functional leadership, stakeholder management, and executive communication.
Proficiency with modern engineering practices — Git/GitHub, CI/CD, automated testing including bench and HIL, boot and performance KPI instrumentation, and large-scale release processes.

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

12+ years of professional experience building embedded or systems software, with a strong foundation in operating system internals, virtualization, or real-time systems.
Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or related fields.
Hands-on background with hypervisor technologies (e.g., Gunyah, QNX Hypervisor, Xen, KVM/ARM) and virtio-based device virtualization, device passthrough, and resource partitioning.
Experience delivering software to ISO 26262 functional safety requirements (up to ASIL-D) and ISO/SAE 21434 cybersecurity requirements.
Depth in secure boot, trusted execution environments, and platform integrity on modern automotive SoCs.
Experience with container runtimes and orchestration in resource-constrained or embedded environments.
Familiarity with Yocto Linux, Android (AOSP/Android Automotive), and QNX SDP as guest or host environments.
Experience with automotive platform standards and practices — Adaptive AUTOSAR, SOAFEE, OTA and continuous update architectures.
Hands-on experience with Qualcomm Automotive SoCs and collaboration with silicon vendors.

new_jobs.title: Senior Manager Service Engineering
new_jobs.description:
The Senior Manager Service Engineering
leads a team dedicated to ensuring products, systems, and equipment are designed and supported for maximum serviceability, minimal downtime, and optimal lifecycle cost. The Senior Manager leads a team of Global Service Engineers responsible for developing service strategies, Service Bills of Material (sBOMs), Level of Repair Analyses (LORA), service documentation requirements, and product improvement initiatives. The manager provides both technical oversight and organizational leadership to embed maintainability principles throughout the product lifecycle.

Responsibilities

Develop and maintain a formal Level of Repair Analysis (LORA) process across all product platforms.
Define repair-versus-replace strategies at the component, assembly, and system levels.
Evaluate repair decisions based on lifecycle cost, reliability, maintainability, service complexity, and customer impact.
Establish repairability standards for major generator subsystems including engines, alternators, control systems, power electronics, fuel systems, and transfer switches.
Utilize LORA outcomes to influence product architecture, service parts strategy, and maintenance planning.
Own the strategy, development, governance, and continuous improvement of Service Bills of Material (sBOMs).
Establish processes for transforming Engineering Bills of Material (eBOMs) into service-ready structures.
Define service assemblies, service kits, replacement components, and maintenance parts required to support products throughout their lifecycle.
Partner with Product Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Product Management to ensure accurate service parts planning.
Ensure service BOM structures are maintained within PLM, ERP, and aftermarket support systems.
Drive service parts simplification and standardization initiatives to optimize inventory and lifecycle support costs.
Establish service parts readiness requirements for all new product introductions.
Design and direct the work of the team.
Select, coach, and develop staff.
Set clear expectations to inspire and motivate the team.
Manage performance by recognizing achievement, providing feedback, and administering progressive discipline when necessary.
Oversee and assign activities and responsibilities for projects assigned to ensure timelines and budgets are met.
Lead Engineers through the implementation of new technologies and equipment.
Define resource needs and works within budget and staffing parameters to accomplish objectives for area of responsibility.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Mechanical, Electrical, or related degree OR 8 years related experience in the Engineering and Service Engineering function within a similar working environment.
10 years’ experience working and supporting a product service organization 5 years of progressive Engineering and/or product service management experience in similar work environment.
Experience with development and maintenance of engineered products.
Experience using SAP/MRP or equivalent ERP.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in Engineering, Technical Management or Business Management.
15 years’ experience with a focus on maintainability, service engineering, or product architecture.
Familiarity with principles and practices of budget preparation and administration.
Experience working with field service operations, service organizations, or aftermarket support.
Deep understanding of maintainability analysis methods, service architecture, and design-for-maintainability best practices.
Demonstrated success implementing maintainability standards across large engineering organizations.

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

Service Bill of Material (sBOM) development and governance.
Level of Repair Analysis (LORA) methodologies.
Design for Serviceability (DFS).
Product Lifecycle Management (PLM).
Service parts strategy and lifecycle support planning.
Warranty and reliability analytics.
Lean principles and continuous improvement methodologies.
Financial acumen and understanding of key business metrics.
Knowledge of GEIA-STD-0007, MIL-STD-1388, or similar standards.
Ability to influence and collaborate across functions.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk and hear; and use hands to manipulate objects or controls. The employee is regularly required to stand and walk. On occasion, the incumbent may be required to stoop, bend, or reach above the shoulders. The employee must occasionally lift up to 25 pounds. Specific conditions of this job are typical of frequent and continuous computer-based work requiring periods of sitting, close vision, and the ability to adjust focus. Occasional travel.
